text:
customer-uptime: Hey @support — our CI started failing when creating new deployments this morning. curl to /v1/projects/abc/deploy returns 403 with body: {"error":"permission_denied","message":"Missing role: deployment.creator"}. Can you help?

support-bot: Thanks for the report — ticket created #INC-8091, pinging eng-oncall. Please paste the curl & response and the token header (redact token).

customer-uptime: Here is the exact repro:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/abc/deploy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1Ni...REDACTED" \
  -d '{"image":"gcr.io/org/app:prod","env":{}}'
```
Response: 403 
```
{"error":"permission_denied","message":"Missing role: deployment.creator","code":403}
```

alexa: @customer-uptime thanks — quick question: is that token a user login token or a service account / OAuth app token?

customer-uptime: It's a service account token minted by our CI (we switched to the new Azure OIDC connector last week).

mike_eng: :eyes: sounds like an OIDC claim mapping/regeneration issue. When the CI exchanged the workload identity for a Redwood token, the "roles" claim might have been dropped. Can you run this to show decoded claims (header only, redact values):
```
echo "eyJhbGciOiJ...REDACTED" | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 --decode | jq .
```

customer-uptime: output (redacted):
```
{"sub":"ci-123","email":"ci@cust.example","groups":["ci-runners"],"aud":"redwood"}
```
No "roles" or "project_roles" claim present.

jen_oncall: That's the smoking gun. Our policy mapping pipeline expects a custom claim (project_roles or roles) when tokens come from federated identity. Looks like the azure OIDC connector is not forwarding the SCIM group->role mapping or the OOB token exchange stripped the custom claim.

ops-ryan: Has this worked previously for that CI service account? Any recent changes to IDP group names or the OIDC app config?

customer-uptime: We renamed a few groups in Azure last weekend as part of cleanup. We thought SCIM would handle it but maybe not.

mike_eng: OK — two paths: short-term workaround and long-term fix. Short-term: create a short-lived service token scoped with deployment.create via Console -> Project -> API tokens (or grant the service account the explicit project role from the UI). That will unblock deploys. Long-term: sync your Azure groups back to the previous names OR update our SCIM mapping so the OIDC exchange emits the project_roles claim.

alexa: I'm adding steps to reproduce for the ticket and tagging identity infra. Also please try a quick manual check on the token exchange endpoint: POST /v1/idp/exchange with your OIDC assertion and see returned claims. Share output (redact secrets).

customer-uptime: Ran exchange, returned token claims same as above — no roles. We still get 200 for login but Redwood treats the token as no privileged roles.

jen_oncall: Internal note for eng: likely regression in the federated-token relayer when the OIDC assertion used groups claim instead of custom claim -> relayer ignores groups unless SCIM mapping present. Filing a follow-up.

mike_eng: For now I can grant the project 'deployment.creator' role to the "ci-runners" group on your project. @alexa can you confirm project id and we can apply the role via backend?

alexa: Confirming project id abc (project slug: abc). @jen_oncall please apply temporary grant to ci-runners group to unblock. We'll remove after customer fixes IDP or confirms mapping.

jen_oncall: Done — I added deployment.creator to group ci-runners on project abc at 2026-03-17T12:34Z (temporary flag set). Can you retry? :lock: :white_check_mark: 

customer-uptime: Retried — deploy now succeeds. Thank you! Can you also document the root cause so we don't get surprises after group renames?

mike_eng: Will do. Follow-up actions: 1) identity infra to check SCIM->role sync for Azure connector, 2) add a validation alert if federated tokens lack project_roles but come from known SCIM tenant, 3) update docs for customers using OIDC: recommend using explicit claim mapping or a dedicated service token if renames are planned.

alexa: I'll create a short KB for support with workaround steps (create scoped service token, temp role grant) and link to it from the ticket.

customer-uptime: Appreciated. One more Q — is there a safe way to rotate group names without downtime?

ops-ryan: Recommend two-step rename: 1) add new group name and map it to roles (dual mapping), 2) migrate CI to new name, 3) remove old mapping. That avoids missing-claim windows. We'll add this to KB.

support-bot: Ticket #INC-8091 updated: status=investigating, owner=eng-oncall, workaround_applied=true.

customer-uptime: Thanks team, moving CI back into green.

mike_eng: Closing loop — we will follow up with identity infra on permanent fix and post KB. Leaving ticket open until mapping confirmed. :thumbsup:
